key_headlines.title: Real Estate Tax Policy Reshapes Market: Luxury Prices Fall While Mid-Range Housing Rises
key_headlines.summary: One year after the August 3 real estate policy implementation, Seoul's high-end properties in Gangnam have declined while mid-to-low-range apartments in outer areas have surged, with some reaching 2 billion won. Property tax burdens are driving 'downsizing' trends in Gangnam reconstruction projects as residents seek smaller units to reduce tax obligations.

key_headlines.title: Acute Rental Housing Shortage Signals Market Structural Problem
key_headlines.summary: Seoul's mega-apartment complexes face near-total depletion of jeonse (lease deposit) listings, with major developments showing only 0.9-3.6% rental supply ratios. Rising real-world monthly rents have hit record highs, with outer districts like Nowon, Dobong, and Gangbuk surpassing 1 million won per month despite falling sales prices.

key_headlines.title: Government Expands EV Subsidies to 430,000 Units with 2 Trillion Won Budget
key_headlines.summary: Facing slowing demand and Chinese EV competition, the government is dramatically increasing electric vehicle purchase subsidies for next year to boost adoption rates and lower consumer burdens. This represents a major policy push amid concerns about Korea's automotive competitiveness.

key_headlines.title: Industrial Metals Surge on AI Infrastructure Demand Despite Supply Constraints
key_headlines.summary: Copper, zinc, and tin prices are rallying as AI infrastructure expansion drives demand for power transmission and advanced electronics materials, while mining supply difficulties create persistent shortages. Copper prices have risen approximately 16% year-to-date with gains reaching 20% from January lows.

key_headlines.title: Democratic Midterm Victory Reshapes US-Korea Trade and Economic Outlook
key_headlines.summary: Democrats secured control of both congressional chambers, but tariff pressures are expected to persist through executive authority via trade acts and targeted measures. Korean industries in shipbuilding, semiconductors, and energy face both challenges and opportunities under this political shift.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's real estate market continues its divergent trajectory with luxury properties declining sharply while mid-to-low-range housing appreciates significantly, creating policy tensions. The acute shortage of jeonse (long-term rental) listings in major apartment complexes is paradoxically driving up monthly rent prices to record levels despite falling sales values. Government initiatives including 2 trillion won in EV subsidies and expanded robot procurement aim to stimulate growth sectors, though implementation challenges persist. Market confidence remains fragile with foreign investor volatility creating unexpected movements in both equity and currency markets. Policy debates intensify between national and city leadership over the actual versus perceived state of housing affordability for ordinary citizens.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The government projects improved fiscal sustainability for next year with the deficit-to-GDP ratio improving from negative 3.8% to negative 0.1%, while the national debt ratio is expected to decline from 51.6% to 48.3% of GDP. Despite double-digit spending increases, fiscal authorities are achieving balance through structural reforms and efficiency improvements. Officials emphasize balancing investment in growth initiatives with long-term fiscal stability, citing first-half GDP growth of 3.8% and expectations of 1 trillion dollar exports and 40,000 dollar per capita income. International context shows divergent policy paths: Australia maintained rate hikes to 4.85% despite economic slowdown, while eurozone inflation reached 4% with energy costs surging 20% due to Middle East tensions. Korea's fiscal approach aims to leverage export recovery momentum while addressing persistent household consumption weakness.
sections.Financial Markets: Korean equity markets exhibited unusual concurrent movements with the won-dollar exchange rate, defying typical forex market dynamics where stock rallies normally accompany currency weakness due to foreign capital inflows. KOSPI ended November 4 with a modest 0.62% gain at 5683.80 points after volatile intraday swings, with retail and institutional investors purchasing 2.25 trillion won while foreigners sold 2.5 trillion won net. Sector performance remained mixed with entertainment and precision medical devices declining significantly. US Treasury yields rose following midterm elections, with 10-year yields at 4.96% and 30-year at 5.33%, reflecting market expectations for economic policies under divided government. Currency volatility and foreign fund flows represent critical risk factors for Korean asset prices moving forward.
sections.Industry & Technology: Government procurement plans to purchase 1,700 robots next year aim to nurture the domestic robotics industry by creating early-stage market demand, leveraging Korea's manufacturing and semiconductor strengths. US midterm election results suggest bipartisan cooperation on shipbuilding, semiconductors, and energy sectors presents new opportunities despite continued tariff pressures on other industries. Mercedes-Benz Korea faced quality issues with electric vehicles using Chinese-sourced batteries, highlighting supply chain vulnerabilities in the EV sector amid competitive pressures. Semiconductor and battery industries face investment pressure and subsidy uncertainty in the US market, with American tax credits and Chinese material restrictions becoming critical variables. Semiconductor equipment orders and delivery timelines may shift depending on actual data center construction schedules in the United States.
sections.Real Estate: Monthly rental prices for Seoul apartments reached record highs in September 2026 at 1.66 million won despite falling sales prices, indicating a structural disconnect between ownership and rental markets that directly increases household rental burden. Gangnam reconstruction projects show accelerating 'downsizing' trends as residents reduce target apartment sizes to decrease tax obligations and increase cash refunds, representing a significant market behavior shift. Daechi-dong experiences acute jeonse shortage ahead of winter vacation period as the Eunma apartment complex announces imminent relocation for reconstruction, with jeonse deposits falling 750 million won in three months. The government introduced Korea's first 'equity accumulation' public housing model in Gwanggyo New City, requiring only partial payment at move-in to acquire housing shares with phased payment completion. Debate intensifies between presidential and mayoral leadership over actual housing affordability realities versus official policy narratives, with outer-district monthly rents exceeding 1 million won across Nowon, Dobong, and Gangbuk areas.
sections.International Economy: Democratic Party control of both US congressional chambers is expected to maintain or intensify tariff policies through executive authorities including Trade Act Sections 301 and 232, limiting Trump's need for new legislation despite power distribution changes. US stock markets rallied over 2% following the election results, with analysis suggesting potential oil price declines if Middle East conflict resolution receives diplomatic priority over energy security concerns. The Trump administration faces economic pressure from rising household living costs driven by tariffs and geopolitical tensions, despite maintaining low unemployment and positive GDP growth metrics. South Africa and Rwanda face tariff preference elimination affecting approximately 10,000 jobs in regions already experiencing 30% unemployment rates, exemplifying targeted trade weaponization. Consumer sentiment in the US reached record lows amid cost-of-living pressures, creating political vulnerability for the incumbent administration despite favorable macroeconomic indicators.
sections.AI & Economy: Industrial metals including copper, zinc, and tin are experiencing significant price appreciation driven by AI infrastructure expansion demands, with copper rising 16% year-to-date as power transmission and advanced electronics manufacturing accelerate. SK Telecom and LG Uplus are accelerating data center investments to capitalize on AI growth opportunities, supplementing traditional telecommunications business recovery with emerging technology sector participation. Korea Electric Power Company emphasizes electricity as fundamental national competitiveness, highlighting how AI and advanced industries are transforming power from industrial input to strategic economic driver. Chinese AI companies face severe chip constraints with access to only approximately 1% of Nvidia's 6 million-unit GPU allocation due to US export controls and Chinese reciprocal import restrictions. US Democratic pressure on data center mega-projects introduces regulatory uncertainty affecting semiconductor and equipment manufacturers' order pipelines and delivery schedules.
sections.Others: US September trade deficit reached 105 billion dollars with modest 0.7% reduction, as exports rose 1.9% driven by capital goods and agricultural products while imports increased 1.2% across computer and related sectors. Future response fund's 45 trillion won budget allocation reveals that major initiatives contain limited genuine growth investment components, with only 3 of 12 major projects clearly targeting advanced industry promotion and startup support. Democratic congressional victories prompt Korean policy makers to reassess US trade and security strategies, particularly regarding operational control handover timelines and implications for bilateral technology cooperation frameworks. Hidden voter sentiment against Trump administration policies manifested in midterm results as living cost pressures and international tensions overshadowed official economic growth metrics. Media analysis suggests 'shy Trump' voter patterns observed in surveys inadequately captured actual electoral behavior driven by household economic anxiety despite favorable headline economic statistics.
